Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which step should come first in this investigation about light bulbs. The options are A) Repeat the investigation, B) Write a report, C) Make a table, and D) Make daily observations. 

First, I think about what's needed when starting an investigation. Usually, you want to gather data before you can analyze it. So, maybe you don't start by writing a report because you don't have data yet. Similarly, making a table without any data might be too early because you don't know what to put in it. 

So that leaves either A or D. But repeating the investigation doesn't make sense as the first step because you're just starting. So that's probably not it. That leaves D) Make daily observations. 

Wait, but why not make a table first? Maybe to organize the data. But if you don't have any data yet, the table would be empty. So it makes more sense to observe the bulbs first to see how they behave before setting up a table. That way, you can capture all the relevant variables you notice during the observations and then create a table based on that information. 

So the first step should be D, making daily observations. That way, you can see how the bulbs fail or how they perform over time, which will help in creating a proper table later on. If you jumped straight to making a table, you might miss important factors that only become clear after some initial observation.
</think>
